newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU formally agrees pact to end U.S. anti-Cuba row.
newsitem.headline: EU formally agrees pact to end U.S. anti-Cuba row.

text.p: European Union member countries formally agreed on Friday to a deal with the United States designed to end a transatlantic row over U.S. anti-Cuba laws.
A statement said that all 15 countries had agreed by written procedure to a plan that would end a disputes panel at the World Trade Organisation (WTO) over the so-called Helms-Burton act.
The act, an amalgam of U.S. anti-Cuba laws, has outraged Washington's trading partners because it threatens non-U.S. businesses with interests in Cuba.

The European Commission and Washington agreed last week to negotiate a compromise in policy towards Cuba under which the EU would drop its WTO complaint and work with the United States toward a global agreement on protection of expropriated property.
The White House would in exchange seek to change a key provision of Helms-Burton barring executives of companies that invest in disputed properties in Cuba from entering the United States.

On Wednesday, EU ambassadors provisionally backed the plan but added a sharply worded statement warning Washington not to renege on the deal. EU governments had until Friday to endorse the ambassadors' decision.

France, Spain, Italy, Portugal and Belgium secured at Wednesday's meeting a clause that any backing of the deal be accompanied with the threat to reopen the WTO disputes panel if Washington took any action against EU companies.
The EU also restated its conclusions of July last year that the U.S. legislation towards Cuba, and other acts targetting Iran and Libya, were unacceptable both in law and principle.

"Nothing in the understanding with the U.S. administration should be regarded as in any way detracting from the continuing approach to these issues set out in those conclusions," Friday's statement said.
